I will keep my full 12 mu in the wheat-maize rotation this year. I am 62, I have only a two-person household, and with 45 years of farming I care more about a steady, manageable system than chasing a more labor-heavy crop. I have well irrigation, so I can support wheat through its key water periods and then carry the land straight into summer maize. Even though I know cotton, on this farm size I would not switch the system this year because wheat-maize is simpler to manage across the whole year, easier to time, and more reliable for output.

For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, put the main fertilizer down up front, irrigate at the key stages, and keep tillage moderate with rotary work because I want a clean seedbed without making the land too hard or spending extra effort on deep ploughing. I will keep pesticide use to what is needed for weeds and disease pressure, not excessive, but enough to protect yield. After wheat harvest, I will move directly into summer maize with hybrid seed because I want stronger yield potential in the shorter summer window. I will fertilize maize a bit more heavily on nitrogen than wheat, use fewer irrigations because of the rainy season and my well backup, and keep field operations simple and timely. My goal is stable yield from both crops over the whole year rather than a complicated plan.
